info.title: Galene.AI Platform - API Documentation
info.description:
Galene is an advanced AI-powered platform for conversational interfaces and intelligent automation.

    ## Authentication
    Most endpoints require authentication via JWT tokens or API keys.
    Use the `/login` endpoint to obtain access tokens.

post.description:
Create a new user account with provided credentials.

Creates a user account in both Keycloak (authentication system) and the local
database. The user is assigned to a default organization and role unless
the caller overrides those values. A temporary password may be set requiring
the user to change it on first login.

**No Authentication Required**: This is a public endpoint for user registration.
**Default Settings**:
- Organization: org_default (or specified)
- Role: 3 (standard user role, or specified)
- Password: Temporary by default, unless `temporary_password` is set to `false`

delete.description:
Disable a user account in the authentication system.

Sets the user's enabled status to False in Keycloak, preventing them from
logging in while preserving all account data. This is a soft delete operation
that can be reversed by re-enabling the account.

**Authentication Required**: User must be authenticated with appropriate permissions.
**Access Control**: Requires admin privileges to disable other users.
**Note**: This disables the account in Keycloak but preserves database records.

Authenticate user with username/email and password.

Validates user credentials through Keycloak and returns authentication tokens
along with user profile information. Handles both regular login and cases
where password reset is required.

**No Authentication Required**: This is the authentication endpoint.
**Returns**: Access token, refresh token, and user profile data
**Special Cases**: Returns password_reset=True if user needs to change password

Log out the current user and invalidate their session.

Invalidates the user's refresh token in Keycloak, effectively logging them
out from all sessions. The access token will continue to work until it expires,
but no new tokens can be generated.

**Authentication Required**: Requires a valid refresh token.

Refresh an expired access token using a valid refresh token.

Generates a new access token and refresh token pair when the current access
token has expired. This allows maintaining user sessions without requiring
re-authentication. Also returns updated user profile information.

**Authentication Required**: Requires a valid refresh token.

post.description:
Complete SSO authentication flow using authorization code.

Exchanges an OAuth2 authorization code received from the SSO provider
for authentication tokens. Creates new user accounts automatically if
they don't exist in the system, assigning them to the specified organization.

**Authentication Flow**:
1. Validates the authorization code with Keycloak
2. Retrieves user information from the SSO provider
3. Creates a new user account if first-time login
4. Returns authentication tokens and user profile

**Auto-Registration**: New users are automatically created with:
- Default role ID from USER_SIGNUP_DEFAULT_ROLE environment variable (default: 3)
- Assignment to the specified organization
- 30-day refresh token validity

**No Authentication Required**: This completes the SSO authentication process.

Returns a list of MASKED API keys created by the current user, including creation
dates and last usage timestamps. API keys are shown in plain text only at creation time.

Generate a new API key for the authenticated user.

Creates a new API key that can be used for programmatic access to the API.
The generated key is unique and securely generated. Users can have multiple
API keys for different applications or purposes.

**IMPORTANT**: The API key is shown in plain text ONLY at creation time.
Save it securely as it cannot be retrieved later. Subsequent GET requests
will show only a masked version of the key.

**Authentication Required**: User must be authenticated via JWT token.
**Security**: API keys are generated using secure random methods.
**Usage**: Use the generated key in the 'Authorization: Bearer <api_key>' header.

Permanently delete an API key owned by the authenticated user.

Removes the specified API key from the system, immediately invalidating it
for future API requests. This action cannot be undone. Applications using
the deleted key will need to be updated with a new key.

**Authentication Required**: User must be authenticated via JWT token.
**Access Control**: Users can only delete their own API keys.

get.description:
Retrieve the SQL query and data-analysis results produced inside a conversation.

When an agent answers a question by querying a database, it stores a data-analysis
result. This endpoint returns that record: the executed SQL query and, when the
agent also ran a pandas analysis, the pandas code — each with a plain-language
explanation in the user's inference language and a downloadable CSV.

**Input**: `conversation_id` from `GET /conversations` (or `/conversation/init`),
and `result_id` which the agent surfaces in its message when a data-analysis result
is available for that conversation.
**`csv_ref`**: a temporary pre-signed download URL for the result CSV, valid for 1 hour.
**`kind`**: `"SQLQuery"` for the raw query result, `"DataAnalysis"` for the pandas step.

**Authentication Required**: User must be authenticated via valid JWT token.
**Access Control**: Only returns results from conversations owned by the user;
otherwise responds with `success: false` and an empty list.

200.description: Results retrieved. Returns `success: false` with an empty `result` list when the conversation, the result record, or its data is not available (no error is raised in these cases).

post.description:
Generate AI responses using the OpenAI Responses API format.

**Available Modes:**
- `shield`: LLM with content filtering (input/output scanning, jailbreak detection). Requires organization-level shield configuration.
- `direct`: LLM without filtering, maximum performance.

**Model Selection:**
The `model` parameter must be a valid model ID from `GET /v1/models` (e.g., `"Galene/LLM"`).
Do NOT pass a conversation UUID — that is only for the chat completions `appliance_shield` mode.

**Reasoning:**
Use `enable_thinking` as the canonical control.
- `enable_thinking: true` keeps thinking enabled.
- `enable_thinking: false` requests instruct/non-thinking behavior.
- `responses.reasoning` is ignored for backend control and kept only for SDK compatibility.

**Tools:**
- **`type: "function"`**: function calling. The model returns `tool_calls`, your client executes them and sends results back.
- **`file_search`**: search across your uploaded documents. Setup:
  1. Upload files with `POST /v1/files`
  2. Create a vector store with `POST /v1/vector_stores`
  3. Add files to it with `POST /v1/vector_stores/{id}/files`
  4. Pass `tools: [{"type": "file_search", "file_search": {"vector_store_ids": ["<vs_id>"]}}]`
  Supports text documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, ...) and images (PNG, JPEG).
- **`web_search` / `web_search_preview`**: search the web and use results to answer.
- **`code_interpreter`**: execute code to answer.

**Streaming:**
Set `stream: true` for Server-Sent Events. The response uses the OpenAI Responses streaming format (event types: `response.created`, `response.output_text.delta`, `response.completed`, etc.).

**Images:**
Inline external image URLs (`input_image` in the `input` field) are NOT supported — the inference server can only access internal presigned URLs. To use images, upload them via `POST /v1/files`, add them to a vector store with `POST /v1/vector_stores`, and use the `file_search` tool. The platform will process them through vision embeddings and inject them as context for the LLM.

Use that id with `GET /v1/files/{file_id}/content` or `DELETE /v1/files/{file_id}`. `store=true` is not supported for streaming responses.

post.description:
Generate vector embeddings for text and/or media input. Fully compatible with OpenAI's /v1/embeddings API for text-only requests.

**Galene Embedding Topologies:**
The backend supports two installation modes.
- `single_multimodal`: the public embeddings model is `Galene/Embedding-Multimodal`, and legacy aliases `Galene/Embedding` / `Galene/Embedding-Vision` are routed internally to the multimodal provider.
- `dual`: `Galene/Embedding` routes to the text-only provider, while `Galene/Embedding-Vision` routes to the multimodal provider.
When using a multimodal-capable model, you can pass an optional `media` field to embed images and videos alongside text. Each text and each media item produces its own independent embedding vector.

**Supported media types:**
- Images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF)
- Videos (MP4, WebM, etc. — embedded as a single vector per video)

**Response ordering:**
- Indices `0` to `len(input)-1`: text embeddings (in input order)
- Indices `len(input)` to `len(input)+len(media)-1`: media embeddings (in order)

**Media input formats:**
- Plain base64 string: `"iVBORw0KGgo..."` (treated as image)
- Object: `{"data": "...", "type": "image|video", "mime_type": "...", "caption": "..."}`

The `caption` guides the vision model on what to focus on. The deprecated `images` field is still accepted for backward compatibility.

**Error handling:**
- Upstream errors preserve their original HTTP status code instead of being flattened to 500.
- Context-length errors are normalized into a structured envelope with `code: "context_length_exceeded"`, a `param` field indicating the offending input (`input` or `media[0]`), and a `details` object containing `input_type`, `required_tokens`, `max_tokens`, and actionable `suggestions` tailored to the detected input type (text, image, video, or mixed media).

post.description:
Generate chat completions using various modes with AI guardrails and safety features.

**Available Modes:**
- `appliance_shield`: Full conversation mode with shield protection. `model` must be a conversation UUID from `POST /conversation`.
- `shield`: LLM with real-time content filtering. `model` must be a model ID from `GET /v1/models`.
- `direct`: LLM without content filtering. `model` must be a model ID from `GET /v1/models`.

**Authentication:**
- Bearer token (JWT from Keycloak login)

configured for that language.

post.description:

for that language, or `502` if the STT service returns no text. Optionally pass a
`language` hint in the body to improve accuracy.

**Input**: `organization_uuid` from `GET /admin/organizations`; the sample must already
be uploaded via `POST /{language_code}`.
**Authentication Required**: Organization admin or superadmin.

patch.description:

The `ref_text` is the transcript of the reference audio, required for voice synthesis.
Provide it manually here (non-empty, otherwise `400`), or generate it automatically via
`POST /{language_code}/transcribe`. Returns `404` if no sample exists for the language.

**Input**: `organization_uuid` from `GET /admin/organizations`; `ref_text` in the body.
**Authentication Required**: Organization admin or superadmin.

get.summary: List groups available for import on the IdP side
get.description:
List the groups available for import from the Identity Provider.

Queries Microsoft Entra (via the Microsoft Graph API) for the live list
of groups in the tenant backing the given SSO connector, and flags which
ones are already imported into this organization.

Path parameters:
- **organization_uuid**: the target organization.
- **connector_uuid**: the Microsoft 365 SSO connector (from the SSO
  connectors list endpoint).

Authentication Required: Organization admin or superadmin.

Errors:
- 503 ``group_sync_disabled`` if the feature kill switch is off.
- 404 ``sso_connector_not_found`` if the connector does not exist.
- 400 ``unsupported_connector_type`` if the connector is not Microsoft 365.
- 400 ``tenant_id_missing`` if the tenant id cannot be resolved.
- 409 ``consent_required`` if the app lacks Microsoft Graph admin consent.
- 502 ``idp_unreachable`` if the Identity Provider cannot be reached.

List the groups already imported into this organization (DB-only).

Returns the imported SSO groups stored locally for the connector,
without contacting the Identity Provider.

Path parameters:
- **organization_uuid**: the target organization.
- **connector_uuid**: the SSO connector (from the SSO connectors list
  endpoint).

Authentication Required: Organization admin or superadmin.

Errors:
- 503 ``group_sync_disabled`` if the feature kill switch is off.
- 404 ``sso_connector_not_found`` if the connector does not exist.

schema.title: Response Get Imported Groups Admin Organizations  Organization Uuid  Sso Connectors  Connector Uuid  Imported Groups Get

put.description:
Declaratively reconcile the set of imported groups for the connector.

Takes the desired list of groups to import and applies it as the new
state: groups not in the payload are removed, new ones are added, and a
role is provisioned for each imported group. The first successful update
also enables group sync for the connector so that subsequent SSO logins
keep group membership in sync.

Path parameters:
- **organization_uuid**: the target organization.
- **connector_uuid**: the Microsoft 365 SSO connector (from the SSO
  connectors list endpoint).

Body:
- **payload**: the desired imported-groups state (``UpdateImportsRequest``).

Authentication Required: Organization admin or superadmin.

Errors:
- 503 ``group_sync_disabled`` if the feature kill switch is off.
- 404 ``sso_connector_not_found`` if the connector does not exist.
- 400 ``unsupported_connector_type`` if the connector is not Microsoft 365.
- 409 ``role_name_collision`` if a group's role name clashes with an
  existing role (the change is rolled back).

post.summary: Resync every SSO user in the organization
post.description:
Resync group membership for every SSO user in the organization.

Iterates over all SSO users in the organization, fetches their current
group membership from Microsoft Entra, and reconciles their assigned
roles against the imported groups. Returns a summary of the run
(users processed, updated, and any per-user errors).

Path parameters:
- **organization_uuid**: the target organization.
- **connector_uuid**: the Microsoft 365 SSO connector (from the SSO
  connectors list endpoint).

Authentication Required: Organization admin or superadmin.

Errors:
- 503 ``group_sync_disabled`` if the feature kill switch is off.
- 404 ``sso_connector_not_found`` if the connector does not exist.
- 400 ``unsupported_connector_type`` if the connector is not Microsoft 365.
- 409 ``consent_required`` if the app lacks Microsoft Graph admin consent.
- 502 ``idp_unreachable`` if the Identity Provider cannot be reached.

get.summary: Probe Microsoft Graph admin consent for this connector
get.description:
Probe whether the connector has the required Microsoft Graph consent.

Performs a lightweight call against Microsoft Graph to determine whether
the app registration backing the connector has been granted the admin
consent and permissions needed for group sync, returning the consent
status and any missing permissions.

Path parameters:
- **organization_uuid**: the target organization.
- **connector_uuid**: the Microsoft 365 SSO connector (from the SSO
  connectors list endpoint).

Authentication Required: Organization admin or superadmin.

Errors:
- 503 ``group_sync_disabled`` if the feature kill switch is off.
- 404 ``sso_connector_not_found`` if the connector does not exist.
- 400 ``unsupported_connector_type`` if the connector is not Microsoft 365.
- 502 ``idp_unreachable`` if the Identity Provider cannot be reached.

get.summary: Generate a Microsoft adminconsent URL with HMAC-signed state
get.description:
Build a Microsoft admin-consent URL with an HMAC-signed state.

Generates the Microsoft Entra ``adminconsent`` URL an administrator can
open to grant the app the Graph permissions required for group sync. The
returned ``state`` is HMAC-signed and bound to the (organization,
connector) pair with a short TTL, so it can be verified on the callback.

Path parameters:
- **organization_uuid**: the target organization.
- **connector_uuid**: the Microsoft 365 SSO connector (from the SSO
  connectors list endpoint).

Authentication Required: Organization admin or superadmin.

Returns a JSON object with the ``url`` and the signed ``state``.

Errors:
- 503 ``group_sync_disabled`` if the feature kill switch is off.
- 404 ``sso_connector_not_found`` if the connector does not exist.
- 400 ``unsupported_connector_type`` if the connector is not Microsoft 365.
- 400 ``tenant_id_missing`` if the tenant id cannot be resolved.

List backup execution logs.

Returns a paginated list of backup execution records (most recent first), including
their status, timing, and messages. Use `page` and `page_size` (1-100) to page through
results; the response includes pagination metadata (`total`, `total_pages`, `has_next`,
`has_prev`). Log IDs from this endpoint can be used to cancel a running backup.

**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

post.description:
Trigger a manual backup run.

Starts an on-demand backup immediately, independent of the configured schedule, using
the current global backup destination and settings. Returns the identifiers of the
started job (`workflow_id`, `workflow_run_id`); progress can be followed via the backup
execution logs endpoint. Responds with `500` if the run could not be started.

**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

Cancel a running backup run.

Requests cancellation of an in-progress backup, identified by its `log_id` (obtained
from the backup execution logs endpoint). Cancellation is cooperative: the run is marked
`CANCEL_REQUESTED` and stops at the next safe point. Responds with `404` if the log id
does not exist, or `409` if the run is not currently running (i.e. not in `RUNNING` or
`CANCEL_REQUESTED` state).

**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

Trigger a manual backup retention cleanup.

Starts an on-demand retention cleanup that removes old backups according to the
configured retention policy, independent of the schedule. Returns the identifiers of the
started job (`workflow_id`, `workflow_run_id`). Responds with `500` if the cleanup could
not be started.

**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

get.description:
List execution traces, with filtering, sorting and pagination.

Returns the recorded traces (one per top-level operation, e.g. a chat completion),
newest first by default. All query parameters are optional filters: `organization_id`,
`conversation_id`, `status`, `name_q` (name search), `user_id`, `tags_any`/`tags_all`
(tag matching), `metadata_contains`, and the `started_after`/`started_before` time
window. Use `limit`/`offset` to page and `sort_dir` (`asc`/`desc`) to order by start time.

Each trace `id` can be used with `GET /observability/traces/{trace_id}` and the
observation/audit sub-resources.

**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

Export the filtered list of traces as a downloadable CSV file.

Accepts the same filters as `GET /observability/traces` and streams the matching
traces as `text/csv`. Use `columns` (comma-separated) to choose and order the output
columns; `limit`/`offset` bound the export (default limit 10000).

**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

get.summary: Get a single trace by ID
get.description:
Retrieve a single trace by its ID.

Returns the full trace record, including its input/output, token usage, status, tags
and metadata. The `trace_id` comes from `GET /observability/traces`.

**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

List the observations recorded under a single trace.

Observations are the individual steps of a trace (LLM calls, tool calls, spans), each
with input/output, timing, token usage and tool details. Optional filters: `type_`,
`status`, `name_q`, `parent_observation_id` (to fetch the children of a step),
`tags_any`/`tags_all`, `metadata_contains`; paginate with `limit`/`offset` and order
with `sort_dir`.

**Input**: `trace_id` from `GET /observability/traces`.
**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

get.summary: Export observations for a trace as CSV
get.description:
Export a trace's observations as a downloadable CSV file.

Accepts the same filters as `GET /observability/traces/{trace_id}/observations` and
streams the matching observations as `text/csv`. Use `columns` (comma-separated) to
select/order columns; `limit`/`offset` bound the export (default limit 20000).

**Input**: `trace_id` from `GET /observability/traces`.
**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

post.summary: Audit a trace read (sensitive content viewed)
post.description:
Record an audit event when a user opens a trace with sensitive content.

Logs that the current user viewed the given trace (timestamp, user, client IP and
user-agent), producing the audit trail returned by
`GET /observability/traces/{trace_id}/reads`. Call it when the trace detail is opened.

**Input**: `trace_id` from `GET /observability/traces`.
**Authentication Required**: Yes.

get.summary: List audit events for a trace read
get.description:
List the read-audit events recorded for a trace.

Returns who viewed the trace and when (user, timestamp, client IP, user-agent) — the
events produced by `POST /observability/traces/{trace_id}/reads`. Optional filters:
`user_id`, the `read_after`/`read_before` time window; paginate with `limit`/`offset`
and order with `sort_dir`.

**Input**: `trace_id` from `GET /observability/traces`.
**Authentication Required**: Yes.

get.summary: Export trace read audit as CSV
get.description:
Export a trace's read-audit events as a downloadable CSV file.

Accepts the same filters as `GET /observability/traces/{trace_id}/reads` and streams
the matching audit events as `text/csv`. `limit`/`offset` bound the export
(default limit 50000).

**Input**: `trace_id` from `GET /observability/traces`.
**Authentication Required**: Superadmin only.

Aggregate usage and guardrail metrics for an organization.

completion / shield tokens, guardrail `blocks` and `warns`, and average trace duration.

be evaluated by a moderation/shield service. It supports either a single
string input or a list of strings, allowing batch moderation requests in
a single object. The optional `model` field is intended to carry the
identifier of the moderation/shield configuration (for example a UUID)

- input: A single text string or a list of text strings to be moderated.
- model: Optional identifier for the moderation/shield configuration to
  apply. If omitted, the user'sorganization default moderation settings will be used.

Example:
    OpenaiChatCompletionRequest(

        model="shield-uuid-1234"
    )

NOTE: inline external image URLs (input_image) are not supported in this field. To use images, upload them via POST /v1/files, add to a vector store via POST /v1/vector_stores, and use the file_search tool — they will be processed through vision embeddings.
examples: What is the capital of France?

model.title: Model

enable_thinking.title: Enable Thinking
enable_thinking.description: Canonical control for thinking mode. Set to true to enable reasoning/thinking output, false to request instruct/non-thinking behavior.

include.title: Include
include.description: Specifies which additional content to include in the response (file search results, images, reasoning traces).

instructions.title: Instructions
instructions.description: Instructions for how the model should behave or respond.
examples: You are a helpful assistant specializing in data analysis.

max_output_tokens.title: Max Output Tokens

metadata.title: Metadata

parallel_tool_calls.title: Parallel Tool Calls
parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use.

previous_response_id.title: Previous Response Id
previous_response_id.description: ID of a previous response for multi-turn conversations. Accepted for SDK compatibility; not functionally used.

reasoning.title: Reasoning
reasoning.description: Reserved for SDK compatibility. This field is ignored by the backend; use enable_thinking for the canonical thinking toggle.

service_tier.title: Service Tier
service_tier.description: The service tier to use for the request. Accepted for SDK compatibility; not functionally used.

store.title: Store
store.description: Whether to store the response for later retrieval. Accepted for SDK compatibility; not functionally used.

stream.title: Stream
stream.description: If true, the response will be streamed as Server-Sent Events.

temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.description: Controls randomness in the response. Higher values (closer to 2) make output more random, lower values (closer to 0) make it more focused.

tool_choice.title: Tool Choice
tool_choice.description: Controls which tools (if any) the model should use. 'auto' lets the model decide, 'none' disables tools.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: A list of tools available to the model during response generation. Supported types: 'function' (client-side execution), 'file_search' (requires vector_store_ids — documents and images must be uploaded via POST /v1/files AND added to a vector store via POST /v1/vector_stores; images are processed through vision embeddings), 'web_search', 'web_search_preview', 'code_interpreter'.

OpenaiResponsesRequest.title: OpenaiResponsesRequest
OpenaiResponsesRequest.description:
OpenAI Responses API Request

Compatible with the OpenAI Responses API format (POST /v1/responses).
Accepts the same parameters as the official OpenAI SDK so that clients
can target this backend without code changes.

Key differences from Chat Completions:
- Input is a string or structured item list (not a messages array).
- Thinking mode is controlled by `enable_thinking`.
- The response uses the Responses format (output array) instead of choices.
